title: Seasoned Spinach
summary: Blanch, squeeze, dress. How hard you squeeze the water out is what decides the flavour.
intro:
Seasoned spinach turns soggy and bland for two reasons, usually: it was blanched too long, or it was not squeezed dry enough.

The blanching time is 30 seconds. Drop the spinach in, turn it once with chopsticks, and that is the time.
steps: Scrape the soil off the root ends of the spinach with the tip of a knife, and if the roots are thick, score them with a cross.
Soak the spinach in water and swish it around, three times over. Grit between the leaves does not come out easily, so submerge and swish rather than rinsing under a tap.
Bring a generous pot of water to a rolling boil and add 1 Tbsp (15 mL) salt.
Lower the spinach in root end first and blanch for 30 seconds. Lift it out as soon as the leaves turn deep green.
Rinse under cold water until all the heat is gone. If it stays lukewarm it keeps cooking and goes limp.
Squeeze it firmly with both hands, until no more water drips out, then cut into 4 cm (1 1/2 in) lengths.
Put the spinach in a bowl, add the soup soy sauce and minced garlic first, and work them through with your hands.
Add the sesame oil and sesame seeds and toss lightly. Taste, and top up with salt if it needs it.
tips: Keep the order: soup soy sauce first, sesame oil after. If the sesame oil coats the leaves first, the seasoning cannot get in.
Winter spinach such as pohangcho has sweet roots, so keep them on and dress them along with the leaves.
Blanched spinach keeps for up to 3 days in the fridge once squeezed. Dress it only just before you eat it.
